issue.title: Conditionally skip blocks
issue.body:
I'd like to skip certain blocks/sections, where the test is performed at runtime. For example, when running on macos in the opam sandbox we can't run any tests that use the network, and when running in a Docker container we might not be able to use IPv6.

Is there a good way to do this already?

If not, what's the best way to implement this? Perhaps if a block raises `Mdx_skip` then it could just be ignored?

issue.title: Add mdx_skip for skipping tests
issue.body:
Fixes #393.

I'm not quite sure where the skipped messages should go. At the moment, they're logged at INFO level, but it might be better to output them to stderr. (update: it now goes to stderr so it works with dune)

Also not sure that the best name is. `skip`, `mdx_skip` and `Mdx.skip` all seem reasonable.

comment.body: This is a very neat solution! mdx_skip seems best to me as a balance between verbose (Mdx.skip) and likely to clash with real code (skip).

issue.title: Fix path representations that are causing expect-like tests to fail in dune 3.24
issue.body:
In https://github.com/ocaml/dune/pull/15156 , release in dune 3.24, the representation of paths was change so that paths would always include their local directory prefix. Test fixtures that depend on the unnormalized representation of paths coming from dune start breaking as a result.

The two changes offered here fix the test breakage reported at https://github.com/realworldocaml/mdx/pull/478#issuecomment-5036254826 and should make https://github.com/realworldocaml/mdx/pull/479 unnecessary for new release.

An alternative approach would be just promote the changes to the file representation into the test fixtures. However, normalizing and fully specifying path representations is the more robust choice if they get printed into text fixtures, IMO.

issue.title: use direct s3 access for source.coop variants when s3fs is available
issue.body:
I had some issues yesterday trying to fetch data from source coop, doing something like:

```python
from geotessera.registry import zarr_store_url
from geotessera.store import GeoTesseraZarr, _zone_for_lon

dataset_version = 'v1.1'
store_url = zarr_store_url(version=dataset_version,)
# store_url='s3://us-west-2.opendata.source.coop/tessera/tessera/zarr/v1.1'
gtz = GeoTesseraZarr(store_url)
```

replacing it with the direct s3 url (commented out above) is of course much faster since it doesn't have to go through the proxy. This PR checks if the user has `s3fs` installed, and modifies the url to direct s3 access for better experience.

I'm not sure if it's the best implementation, you may want to make this optional in `store.GeoTesseraZarr` for testing purposes.

comment.body: Agreed, let's go with this until the proxy is debugged!

issue.title: zarr: use floor not round when placing tiles, fixing one-pixel nodata seams
issue.body:
Fixes #429.

Each tile's transform comes from project_tile, which projects the corners of
the 0.1 degree cell. Those corners are arbitrary numbers, not multiples of
10 m. The pixels inside the npy were produced by stackstac, which snaps its
grid down to a multiple of 10 m first. So the transform says one thing and
the pixels sit slightly elsewhere.

The zone grid origin is snapped the same way stackstac snaps, so the right
way to work out where a tile goes is to round down. _tile_pixel_offset
rounded to nearest instead. The two agree while the fraction is under half a
pixel and differ by one pixel above it, separately in x and y. About three
quarters of tiles were therefore placed 10 m too far east, too far south, or
both.

Where a shifted tile sat next to an unshifted one, the column or row between
them was written by neither and kept the +inf nodata fill. Those are the
seams in the issue.

Here are the two tiles either side of the reported seam, utm17 at lon -79.30,
against the published grid origin:

    grid_-79.35_-0.55   fraction 0.354   round 50838   floor 50838   width 1113
    grid_-79.25_-0.55   fraction 0.508   round 51952   floor 51951   width 1114

The west tile finishes at column 51951. Rounding starts the east tile at
51952 and leaves 51951 empty. Flooring starts it at 51951 and the two touch.
That fraction is only just over a half, which is why seams appear at some
tile boundaries and not at most of them.

The test added here is that same pair of tiles, and it fails on the old code.

This fixes new conversions only. Stores already built keep the offset and the
seams and would need converting again. The npy tiles themselves are fine; the
mistake was only in where the converter put them.

comment.body: Thanks Windows CI breakage is a separate issue on main, which I'll fix

issue.title: Nodata seams in v1.0 and v1.1 cambridge variants
issue.body:
Hi again folks, doing some more exploration in Ecuador, I found some nodata seams in the Cambridge variants. I couldn't check in some of the other variants because it's one of the sparsely observed areas related to #424 . It doesn't seem to happen for most seams, but happy to run something that systematically checks them to characterise the extent of the issue if somebody can point me to a spatial file with the grid described in it. There does not appear to be any missing data in the `npy` dataset, so I think this is introduced at some point during the stitching and conversion to `Zarr`. Code to reproduce this particular area for the Zarr dataset:
```python import numpy as np from geotessera.registry import zarr_store_url from geotessera.store import GeoTesseraZarr, _zone_for_lon from pyproj import Transformer LON, LAT = -79.2999134, -0.5891347 HALF_M = 150 # window half-width in metres def report(dataset_variant: str, dataset_version: str) -> None: print(f"\n=== {dataset_variant} ({dataset_version}) ===") store_url = zarr_store_url(version=dataset_version, variant=dataset_variant, ) gtz = GeoTesseraZarr(store_url) zone = _zone_for_lon(LON) ds = gtz.open_zone(zone=zone) transformer = Transformer.from_crs("EPSG:4326", ds.tessera.crs, always_xy=True) easting, northing = transformer.transform(LON, LAT) print(f"UTM zone {zone}, e={easting:.1f}, n={northing:.1f}, crs={ds.tessera.crs}") window = ds.sel( x=slice(easting - HALF_M, easting + HALF_M), y=slice(northing + HALF_M, northing - HALF_M), ) scales = window["scales"].compute() for year, scales_year in zip(scales["time"].values, scales.values): nodata = np.isposinf(scales_year) water = np.isnan(scales_year) # cols = sorted(set(np.nonzero(nodata)[1].tolist())) print( f" {year}: shape={scales_year.shape}, nodata(+inf)={int(nodata.sum())}" ) report("cambridge", "v1.1") report("cambridge", "v1.0") ``` ``` === cambridge (v1.1) === UTM zone 17, e=689195.1, n=-65146.0, crs=EPSG:32617 ... 2023: shape=(30, 30), nodata(+inf)=30 2024: shape=(30, 30), nodata(+inf)=30 2025: shape=(30, 30), nodata(+inf)=30 ... ```
The screenshot below shows the line on a false color RGB of the first three dimensions of the feature vector, although the line here is two pixels wide instead of one due to a reprojection to a conical equal area projection to stitch together two UTM zones: I'm having some issues with source cooperative at the moment dropping connections at the moment, so I'll do some more exploring tomorrow. Let me know if there's any more checks I can do to help with this. Cheers! K.
